questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All gels are boats.

All pumps are boats.

All boats are ships.

**Conclusions:**

I. All pumps are ships.

II. All ships are gels.

III. Some ships are pumps.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/350131873faa477eff3b516f1e1bac12f57b28993f5034add778cdebe4d42887.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All pumps are ships → Follow (As, all pumps are boats and all boats are ships. So, as whole pumps comes in boats which whole comes in ships, therefore it is definitely true.)

II. All ships are gels → Does not follow (As, all gels are boats and all boats are ships. So, it is possible but not definitely true.)

III. Some ships are pumps → Follow (As, all pumps are boats and all boats are ships. So, as whole pumps comes in boats which whole comes in ships, therefore it is definitely true.)

So, Only conclusions I and III follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusions I and III follow".

questions.question: Bank rate is the rate at which:

options.text: Central Bank borrows loan from Government
Commercial banks lend loan to Central bank
Commercial banks lend loan to Government
Central bank lends loan to commercial banks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Central Bank lends loan to commercial banks.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Bank rate:

 
 
• Bank rate is a rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides the loan to commercial banks without keeping any security.
 
• There is no agreement on repurchase that will be drawn up or agreed upon with no collateral as well.
 
• The RBI allows short-term loans with the presence of collateral.
 
• This is known as Repo Rate.
 
• Bank Rates in India is determined by the RBI.
 
• It is usually higher than a Repo Rate on account of its ability to regulate liquidity.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Monetary Policy:

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act) was amended by the Finance Act, 2016, to provide for a statutory and institutionalized framework for a Monetary Policy Committee, for maintaining price stability, while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• The Monetary Policy Committee is entrusted with the task of fixing the benchmark policy rate (repo rate) required to contain inflation within the specified target level.
 
• The Government of India, in consultation with RBI, notified the ‘Inflation Target’ in the Gazette of India dated 5 August 2016 for the period beginning from the date of publication of the notification and ending on March 31, 2021, as 4%.
 
• At the same time, lower and upper tolerance levels were notified to be 2% and 6% respectively.
 
 
 
• Instruments of monetary policy:
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):
 
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio is a specified amount of bank deposits which banks are required to keep with the RBI in the form of reserves or balances.
 
• The higher the CRR with the RBI, the lower will be the liquidity in the system and vice versa.
 
• The CRR was reduced from 15% in 1990 to 5 % in 2002.
 
• The current CRR is 3.00%.
 
 
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
 
 
• All financial institutions have to maintain a certain quantity of liquid assets with themselves at any point in time of their total time and demand liabilities.
 
• This is known as the Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
 
• The assets are kept in non-cash forms such as precious metals, bonds, etc.
 
• The current percentage of SLR is 18%.
 
 
 
• Bank Rate Policy:
 
 
• Also known as the discount rate, bank rates are interest charged by the RBI for providing funds and loans to the banking system.
 
• An increase in bank rate increases the cost of borrowing by commercial banks which results in the reduction in credit volume to the banks and hence the supply of money declines.
 
• An increase in the bank rate is the symbol of the tightening of the RBI monetary policy.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.

questions.question: The term Stumping is related to which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Stumping is a term used in cricket when the wicket-keeper catches the ball and removes the bails before the batsman can return to the crease.
 
• It is a common way of dismissing batsmen in cricket.
 
• Stumps
 
 
• Three vertical posts serve as the stumps and hold up two bails. At each end of the pitch, a wicket is created by the combination of the stumps and bails, which are typically constructed of wood, most frequently ash.
 
• Each stump is identified with a unique name:
 
 
• Off stump is the stump that is on the other side of the wicket from the batsman.
 
• The middle of the three stumps is referred to as the middle stump.
 
• The leg stump is the stump that is on the same side as the batsman's legs as the wicket.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In baseball, a similar term is used called "tagging out" where a fielder touches the base with the ball before the runner reaches it.
 
• In tennis, stumping has no relevance as it is an individual sport and there is no wicket-keeper involved.-Basketball also has no relation to stumping as there are no wickets or bails involved in the game.

questions.question: The least multiple of 7, which leaves a remainder of 4, when divided by 6, 9, 15 and 18 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 9, so its sum of digits must also leave a remainder of 4 when divided by 9.

Checking the sum of digits for the given options:

364 → 3 + 6 + 4 = 13 → 13 ÷ 9 leaves remainder 4.

357 → 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 → 15 ÷ 9 leaves remainder 6.

Only 364 satisfies this condition and is also perfectly divisible by 7 (364 ÷ 7 = 52).

**∴ The correct answer is 364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 6, 9, 15, and 18

Remainder in each case = 4

The number is perfectly divisible by 7.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = LCM(Divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 6, 9, 15, and 18 = 90

⇒ The required number must be of the form: N = 90k + 4

⇒ We are given that N is perfectly divisible by 7.

⇒ Let us break 90k into multiples of 7: N = 84k + 6k + 4

⇒ Since 84k is a multiple of 7, the remaining term (6k + 4) must also be completely divisible by 7.

⇒ Let us check for the minimum integer values of k:

⇒ For k = 1, 6(1) + 4 = 10 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 2, 6(2) + 4 = 16 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 3, 6(3) + 4 = 22 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 4, 6(4) + 4 = 28 (Divisible by 7)

⇒ Substitute k = 4 into the general form equation:

⇒ N = 90 × 4 + 4 = 360 + 4 = 364

**∴ The correct answer is 364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Remainder Rule

If a number leaves a common remainder R when divided by x, y, and z, the number is always of the form N = LCM(x, y, z) × k + R.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9. The remainder when a number is divided by 9 is exactly the same as the remainder when its digital sum is divided by 9.

Divisibility by 7

To check divisibility by 7, double the last digit and subtract it from the rest of the number. If the final result is a multiple of 7, the original number is also divisible by 7.

⇒ Speed in still water = (7.56 + 4.2)/2 = 5.88 km/hr

**Therefore, the rowing speed in still water is approximately 5.88 km/hr.**
